subject: Context length & token volumes — pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Context length profiling for pricing — post-call recap + next steps

Alex — thanks again for a great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size pricing: 

Call recap (my notes)
- Primary use case: document Q&A and long-form summarization for customer support and compliance audits.
- Typical input: stitched transcripts + logs + metadata; average raw document length ~45k characters (~7–9k tokens) but there are outliers up to ~110k chars (~20–25k tokens).
- Output: concise summaries + extraction fields; average completion length ~400–800 tokens depending on task.
- Traffic profile: 3–4k users active, peak concurrent requests ~80–120, predicted monthly requests ~1.2M, avg per-request prompt tokens ~1,200, avg completion ~600. Estimated monthly tokens = (1.2M * (1,200 + 600)) ~ 2.16B tokens monthly.

Key pricing inputs we need confirmed from you:
1) Average prompt tokens per request (you mentioned 1k–1.5k; can you confirm a rounded avg?)
2) Average completion tokens (you mentioned ~500–700; is 600 reasonable?)
3) Percent of requests that need >8k context vs >32k vs >128k (ballpark split helps us recommend model/quantization).
4) Target unit economics / target $ per 1M tokens (you mentioned $X/1M as a budget target) and any contractual/po constraints.

Proposed next steps
- You: Share a short sample of anonymized token-length profile (CSV or summary) and confirm target $/1M tokens.
- Us: I’ll share a tailored pricing sheet (attached) with modeled unit economics for 8k/32k/128k contexts and a recommended deployment (hosted vs dedicated) and concurrency guidance.
- If you want, Jordan can run a quick throughput/latency estimate for your concurrency profile.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf (pricing examples), context_length_sample_stats.csv (example format)

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Context length profiling for pricing — post-call recap + next steps

Marissa — thanks for the notes, this is very helpful. Quick answers below: 

1) Avg prompt tokens: we ran a sample across 10k requests — mean 1,150 tokens, median 980, 90th percentile ~2,800 (mainly because of long transcripts). 1,200 as a rounded avg is fine.
2) Avg completion tokens: 620 average across summarization/QA mix.
3) Context needs: approx breakdown: 78% fit within 8k, 18% require 32k, ~4% would need 128k (these are legal audit bundles).
4) Budget target: leadership is targeting ~$30–40 / 1M tokens for initial PO evaluation (they asked for unit economics target rather than list price).

We can share an anonymized CSV of token lengths by request later today. Procurement may want a 12-month forecast (we can estimate from your modeled pricing).

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of ML Products | Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Context length profiling for pricing — post-call recap + next steps

Alex — great, that breakdown is perfect and very actionable. Based on those numbers here are the modeled unit economics and recommended options (high-level):

Assumptions from your data: avg prompt = 1,200 tokens, avg completion = 620 tokens, monthly requests = 1.2M => monthly token usage ~2.184B (close to your estimate). Context split: 78% 8k, 18% 32k, 4% 128k.

Modeled pricing (example; see attached sheet for full line items) 
- Hosted API (per-token billing, no reserved capacity):
  - 8k-capable model path: $45 / 1M tokens equivalent (for this workload profile)
  - 32k-capable model path (higher memory / slower batching): $60 / 1M tokens
  - 128k-capable path (rare larger contexts, dedicated allocations): $110 / 1M tokens
  Blended price estimate (using your context split) = 0.78*$45 + 0.18*$60 + 0.04*$110 = ~$51.4 / 1M tokens

- Dedicated (reserved capacity) example: with a 12-month commit and predictable 2.2B tokens/month, we can offer tiered unit economics:
  - Effective blended: ~$36–40 / 1M tokens depending on commit level and concurrency profile (includes autoscaling buffer + workload-specific batching).

Other notes / tradeoffs:
- Batching & KV caching: For your workload, enabling prefix caching on repeated documents and smarter batching for the 8k cases will reduce effective cost by ~8–12% and improve throughput.
- Latency/Concurrency: Jordan — can you confirm whether 120 peak concurrent requests are evenly distributed (spiky bursts) or if they tend to queue? This affects pod sizing.
- Contract ask: If Acme wants a target unit economics of $30–40 / 1M tokens, Dedicated with a 12-month committed commit looks like the right path; we can model exact numbers if you share a 12-month forecast.

Next steps (proposed)
- Alex: share the anonymized CSV (sample token length per request) and a 12-month forecast by EOD.
- Jordan: will produce a latency/concurrency sizing note for the 120 concurrent profile and expected pods.
- Me: I’ll update the pricing sheet and send a draft contract language for a 12-month reserved capacity that hits the $36–40 / 1M blended target (assuming forecast holds).

Attachment: updated redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf (line-item model)

Thanks — Marissa
